note: The work registry. Drives ingest, the reader, the library, and the rights gate. `tier` is the rights/quality tier (A = clean PD, full reader; B = PD but rough OCR, excerpt reader labelled as reflowed; C = in copyright or unquotable, NEVER a reader unit). `corpus` names the matching file in arthur/index/_corpus, which is the quote-validation substrate. `voice` matches arthur/base.json author names.

works.title: Le Morte d'Arthur
works.author: Sir Thomas Malory
works.edition: Caxton's text of 1485, as edited for Project Gutenberg
works.blurb: The keystone. A knight-prisoner compiled the French and English streams into one tragic English book and counted the cost of every motif he inherited — the only voice that touches all seven throughlines.

works.title: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
works.author: the Gawain poet
works.edition: Retold in modern prose by Jessie L. Weston (1898)
works.blurb: The whole chivalric code put on trial in one knight, one year, and one concealed green girdle — the flaw no oath can legislate away.

works.title: The Mabinogion — the Arthurian tales
works.author: anonymous (Welsh)
works.blurb: The Celtic root: a war-band Arthur surrounded by impossible tasks, and a Peredur who sees the bleeding spear go by and says nothing.

works.title: Four Arthurian Romances
works.author: Chrétien de Troyes
works.blurb: The inventor of Arthurian romance — and, almost in passing, of the Lancelot–Guinevere love. His Grail poem, the Conte du Graal, is not here: no clean public-domain English translation exists.

works.title: The High History of the Holy Graal
works.author: anonymous (Old French)
works.blurb: The strangest and most violent of the Grail romances: a Grail bound up with bloodshed and the changing of the Law.

parse.bodyStart: \nTHE HIGH HISTORY OF THE HOLY GRAAL\n

works.title: Parzival
works.author: Wolfram von Eschenbach
works.blurb: The humane counter-voice: a Grail that is a stone, and a wounded king cured not by purity or doctrine but by one question asked out of pity.

works.title: Roman de Brut
works.author: Wace
works.blurb: The chronicler who invented the Round Table — as a piece of engineering against precedence, so that no man could boast he was exalted above his fellow.

works.title: Layamon's Brut
works.author: Layamon
works.blurb: The first Arthur in English, and the first to send the wounded king to the elf-queen Argante in Avalon — with the promise that he would come again.

works.title: Historia Brittonum
works.author: Nennius
works.blurb: The earliest list of Arthur's twelve battles — where legitimacy is not election or descent but simply victory.

parse.bodyEnd: \nTHE GENEALOGY OF THE KINGS OF KENT\.\n

works.title: Idylls of the King
works.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
works.blurb: The Victorian reception: Camelot rises and rots, and the Grail quest is the thing that ruins the order. Included as reception, not as a medieval witness.

works.title: The History of the Kings of Britain
works.author: Geoffrey of Monmouth
works.edition: Translated by Sebastian Evans (1903); archive.org scan
works.blurb: The founder. Turned a Welsh war-leader into a king of Britain and gave the legend its political skeleton — and Merlin's prophecies as a dynastic charter.
works.rights: Public domain. Text reflowed from the research base's OCR corpus; original pagination and paragraphing are lost.
works.tier_note: Served as excerpts sliced at the base's book/chapter anchors. The underlying text is OCR of a 1903 translation: readable and citeable, but re-flowed rather than typeset.

works.title: The Quest of the Holy Grail
works.author: anonymous (Old French)
works.edition: Translated by W. W. Comfort (1926); archive.org scan
works.blurb: The Grail as judgment: only the cleansed may approach, and the quest is a purge that sorts the saved from the damned. The take the Vulgate seeds and Malory mourns, here speaking in its own voice.
works.rights: Public domain. Quotations only; the OCR is too uneven for a reader.
works.tier_note: Searchable and quotable at short length; not published as a reading text.

works.title: Tristan
works.author: Gottfried von Strassburg
works.edition: Translated by Jessie L. Weston (1899); archive.org scan
works.blurb: The other adultery, and the one that cannot be repented — because the potion means it was never chosen.
works.tier_note: Searchable and quotable at short length; not published as a reading text.

works.title: Syr Gawayn and the Grene Kny3t
works.author: the Gawain poet
works.edition: Richard Morris's EETS edition of the Cotton Nero A.x manuscript (1864)
works.blurb: The poem as it survives: one manuscript, in a north-west Midland dialect, with thorns and yoghs intact.
works.rights: Public domain. Project Gutenberg #14568. Held as the quotation source for the poem's own words.
works.tier_note: The Middle English is quoted here but not published as a reading text: this portal serves Weston's modern prose so the poem can actually be read, and keeps the original for quotation, since a translation cannot be quoted as the poet's words.

works.title: Syr Gawayne — the Madden romances
works.author: anonymous (Middle English)
works.edition: Sir Frederic Madden, Syr Gawayne (1839): the Wedding of Dame Ragnell, the Awntyrs off Arthure, Golagros and Gawane, the Carle of Carlisle
works.blurb: The rest of Gawain's afterlife in English: the Loathly Lady who answers what women most desire, a ghost on the Tarn Wathelene, and the limits of Arthur's conquest.
works.rights: Public domain, but the 1839 blackletter scan is too rough to publish or quote at length.
works.tier_note: Madden's 1839 type — long s read as f, heavy abbreviation — defeats the quotation gate outright. The Wedding of Dame Ragnelle is quoted here from a small hand-checked transcription of the riddle and its answer; the rest of the volume is searchable but not quotable, and that is a limitation rather than a choice.

works.title: Six Old English Chronicles
works.author: Gildas, Nennius and others
works.blurb: The oldest witness, and a famous silence: Gildas describes the British victory at Badon within living memory of it and never names Arthur.
works.rights: Public domain. Held for the Gildas material; Nennius and Geoffrey are published separately from better texts.
works.tier_note: Kept as a search and validation source only, to avoid publishing a second, inferior text of Nennius and Geoffrey alongside the ones this portal already sets.

works.title: The English Mortes
works.author: anonymous (Middle English)
works.edition: Alliterative Morte Arthure (Brock, EETS) and the Stanzaic Le Morte Arthur (Hemingway)
works.blurb: Malory's own English sources for the fall: Fortune's wheel in the alliterative poem, the love-and-death of the fellowship in the stanzaic one.
works.rights: Public domain, but the OCR of the Middle English is too rough to publish or to quote at length.
works.tier_note: Searchable in the research base; quote-pending. Named here rather than hidden.

works.title: Lancelot-Grail (the Vulgate Cycle)
works.author: anonymous (Old French)
works.edition: Translated by Norris J. Lacy et al.
works.blurb: The systematiser: romance welded to theology in a vast prose cycle with a doom built into its architecture. Malory's main source.
works.rights: IN COPYRIGHT. Used for research and quote validation only; never redistributed here. Short quotations appear under fair use with translator and locus. See DECISIONS.md ADR-0004.
works.tier_note: The only modern translation of the cycle is in copyright, so the Vulgate can be quoted here but not read here. That is a real limitation, and it is stated rather than hidden.
